title: Module 4: Objects, Prototypes & Prototypal Delegation (All Chapters)
description: Comprehensive module-level assessment covering all chapters of Module 4: Objects, Prototypes & Prototypal Delegation.

cards.concept: Object Literals & Constructor Functions: Prototypal Delegation & Prototype Chain
cards.question: When evaluating `obj.property`, what sequence does the JavaScript runtime follow across the prototype chain?

options.text: It queries constructor static properties first, then the global scope.
It checks own property descriptors on `obj`, then steps through `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)` upward until finding the property or reaching `null`.
It checks `Object.prototype` first, and cascades down.
It executes getters on all registered subclasses concurrently.

cards.explanation: Property resolution checks the object's own property table first. If not found, it traverses upward via the [[Prototype]] internal link until it finds the property or reaches null.
cards.pitfall: Modifying Object.prototype directly introduces security risks (prototype pollution) and deoptimizes V8 hidden classes across all objects.
cards.citation: ECMAScript 2024 Specification §10.1.8 / MDN Web Docs: Inheritance and prototype chain

cards.concept: Object Literals & Constructor Functions: Object.create(null) for Pure Dictionaries
cards.question: Why is `Object.create(null)` preferred over a plain object literal `{}` when creating secure string-to-value dictionary lookups?

options.text: It compresses values with gzip in memory.
It has no [[Prototype]] link and inherits zero properties (such as toString, constructor, __proto__), preventing key collisions and prototype pollution.
It runs in constant O(1) time regardless of map size.
It automatically freezes all nested properties.

cards.explanation: Object.create(null) produces an object with no prototype chain. It does not inherit hasOwnProperty or __proto__, preventing attacks where user input keys match inherited prototype properties.
cards.pitfall: Calling dict.hasOwnProperty(key) directly throws TypeError because hasOwnProperty is not inherited; use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(dict, key) or Object.hasOwn().
cards.citation: MDN Web Docs: Object.create() / TC39 Object.hasOwn()
